name: English: Memorize 114 working translation
src: Mafātīḥ al-Jinān (al-Qummī), from al-Ṭūsī's Miṣbāḥ al-Mutahajjid. Text checked word by word against three independent digital editions; variants noted.

v.1: O Allah, I ask You by Your mercy, which encompasses all things,
v.2: and by Your power, by which You have subdued all things, before which all things are humbled, and before which all things are abased,
v.3: and by Your omnipotence, by which You have overcome all things, and by Your might, which nothing can withstand,
v.4: and by Your grandeur, which has filled all things, and by Your authority, which towers over all things,
v.5: and by Your Face, which remains after all things pass away, and by Your Names, which have filled the pillars of all things,
v.6: and by Your knowledge, which encompasses all things, and by the light of Your Face, by which all things are lit.
v.7: O Light, O All-Holy, O First of the first, and O Last of the last!
v.8: O Allah, forgive me the sins that tear apart protections.
v.9: O Allah, forgive me the sins that bring down retribution.
v.10: O Allah, forgive me the sins that change blessings.
v.11: O Allah, forgive me the sins that hold back supplication.
v.12: O Allah, forgive me the sins that bring down affliction.
v.13: O Allah, forgive me every sin I have committed and every error I have made.
v.14: O Allah, I seek nearness to You through Your remembrance, and I seek Your intercession with Yourself,
v.15: and I ask You, by Your generosity, to draw me near to You, to enable me to thank You, and to inspire me to remember You.
v.16: O Allah, I ask You with the asking of one humble, abased and lowly, that You pardon me and have mercy on me,
v.17: and make me pleased and content with what You have apportioned, and humble in every state.
v.18: O Allah, and I ask You with the asking of one whose poverty is severe, who has laid his need before You in hardship, and whose longing for what is with You is great.
v.19: O Allah, Your authority is mighty, Your place is exalted, Your plan is hidden, Your command is manifest,
v.20: Your subjugation prevails, Your power runs its course, and there is no escaping Your rule.
v.21: O Allah, I find no forgiver for my sins, no concealer of my ugly deeds, and none to change any of my ugly acts into good, other than You.
v.22: There is no god but You; glory and praise be to You. I have wronged myself, and I have been bold in my ignorance,
v.23: and I have relied on Your remembering me of old and Your favour to me.
v.24: O Allah, my Protector, how many ugly deeds You have covered, how many crushing afflictions You have lifted,
v.25: how many stumbles You have shielded me from, how many misfortunes You have turned away,
v.26: and how much fine praise You have spread of me that I did not deserve!
v.27: O Allah, my affliction is great, my bad state has gone too far, my deeds have fallen short,
v.28: my shackles have held me down, and my far-off hopes have kept me from what benefits me.
v.29: The world has deceived me with its delusions, and my soul with its offences and its delaying.
v.30: My Master, I ask You by Your might not to let my bad deeds and actions veil my supplication from You,
v.31: and do not expose me for the hidden secrets of mine that You know,
v.32: and do not hasten to punish me for what I have done in private — my bad actions and my wrongdoing,
v.33: my constant negligence and ignorance, and my many desires and my heedlessness.
v.34: And be, O Allah, by Your might, kind to me in every state and compassionate to me in every affair.
v.35: My God and my Lord, whom do I have but You, to ask to remove my distress and look into my affairs?
v.36: My God and my Protector, You set a law for me, and in it I followed my own desire,
v.37: and I did not guard against my enemy's enticement; so he deceived me through what I desired, and fate assisted him in that.
v.38: So, through what befell me in that, I overstepped some of Your limits and disobeyed some of Your commands.
v.39: So praise belongs to You, against me, in all of that,
v.40: and I have no argument in what Your decree brought upon me, and in what Your ruling and Your trial imposed on me.
v.41: And now I have come to You, my God, after my shortcomings and my excess against myself,
v.42: apologising, regretful, broken, asking release, asking forgiveness, turning back, acknowledging, submitting, confessing.
v.43: I find no escape from what I have done, and no refuge to turn to in my affair,
v.44: except Your accepting my excuse and admitting me into the breadth of Your mercy.
v.45: O Allah, so accept my excuse, have mercy on my severe distress, and free me from my tight bonds.
v.46: My Lord, have mercy on the weakness of my body, the thinness of my skin, and the brittleness of my bones.
v.47: O You who began my creation, my mention, my upbringing, my care and my nourishment,
v.48: forgive me for the sake of Your first generosity and Your earlier kindness to me.
v.49: My God, my Master and my Lord! Would You punish me with Your fire after I have professed Your oneness,
v.50: and after my heart has embraced knowledge of You, and my tongue has constantly mentioned You,
v.51: and my conscience has held fast to love of You, and after my sincere confession and supplication, humbled before Your lordship?
v.52: Far from it! You are too generous to abandon one You have nurtured, or to banish one You have drawn near,
v.53: or to drive away one You have sheltered, or to hand over to affliction one You have protected and shown mercy.
v.54: I wish I knew, my Master, my God and my Protector,
v.55: will You give the Fire power over faces that have fallen prostrate before Your grandeur,
v.56: and over tongues that have sincerely declared Your oneness and praised You with thanks,
v.57: and over hearts that have acknowledged Your divinity with conviction,
v.58: and over consciences that have gathered such knowledge of You that they have become humble,
v.59: and over limbs that have hastened obediently to the places of Your worship and gestured submissively for Your forgiveness?
v.60: This is not what is thought of You, nor what we have been told of Your bounty, O Generous One!
v.61: My Lord, You know my weakness before even a little of the trials and punishments of this world
v.62: and the hardships that befall its people,
v.63: even though that is a trial and a hardship whose stay is short, whose duration is brief, whose period is fleeting.
v.64: So how can I bear the trial of the Hereafter and the great hardships that occur in it?
v.65: It is a trial whose period is long, whose stay is lasting, and which is not lightened for its people,
v.66: because it comes only from Your wrath, Your retribution and Your anger,
v.67: and this is something the heavens and the earth cannot withstand.
v.68: My Master, then how will it be for me, while I am Your servant — weak, lowly, worthless, poor and wretched?
v.69: My God, my Lord, my Master and my Protector! For which things do I complain to You,
v.70: and over which of them do I cry out and weep: the pain and severity of the punishment, or the length and duration of the trial?
v.71: If You consign me to the punishments with Your enemies, and put me together with the people of Your trial,
v.72: and separate me from Your loved ones and Your friends,
v.73: then suppose, my God, my Master, my Protector and my Lord, that I could endure Your punishment — how could I endure being parted from You?
v.74: And suppose I could endure the heat of Your fire — how could I endure being kept from gazing at Your grace?
v.75: Or how could I dwell in the Fire while my hope is Your pardon?
v.76: By Your might, my Master and my Protector, I swear sincerely: if You leave me able to speak, I will cry out to You among its people with the cry of the hopeful,
v.77: and I will scream to You with the scream of those who call for help, and weep for You with the weeping of the bereaved,
v.78: and I will call out to You: Where are You, O Guardian of the believers, O utmost hope of those who know You,
v.79: O Rescuer of those who seek rescue, O Beloved of the hearts of the truthful, and O God of the worlds!
v.80: Would You — glory and praise be to You, my God — hear in it the voice of a Muslim servant imprisoned there for his disobedience,
v.81: who has tasted its punishment for his sin, and is confined between its layers for his crime and offence,
v.82: while he cries out to You with the cry of one who hopes for Your mercy, calls You with the tongue of the people of Your oneness, and seeks Your help through Your lordship?
v.83: My Protector, how could he remain in the punishment while he hopes for Your forbearance of old?
v.84: Or how could the Fire hurt him while he hopes for Your bounty and Your mercy?
v.85: Or how could its flames burn him while You hear his voice and see his place?
v.86: Or how could its roaring engulf him while You know his weakness?
v.87: Or how could he be tossed between its layers while You know his sincerity?
v.88: Or how could its keepers drive him back while he calls out to You, “O Lord”?
v.89: Or how could he hope for Your bounty in freeing him from it, and You leave him there?
v.90: Far from it! That is not what is thought of You, nor what is known of Your bounty, nor like the kindness and goodness You have shown those who profess Your oneness.
v.91: I declare with certainty: were it not for what You have decreed — punishing those who deny You — and what You have ordained — keeping those who stubbornly oppose You there forever —
v.92: You would have made the Fire, all of it, coolness and safety, and no one would have had a resting place or an abode in it.
v.93: But You — holy are Your Names — have sworn to fill it with the disbelievers, of jinn and humankind together,
v.94: and to keep those who stubbornly oppose You there forever. And You — majestic is Your praise — said, beginning the favour and bestowing it out of generosity:
v.95: “Is one who is a believer like one who is a transgressor? They are not equal.”
v.96: My God and my Master, I ask You by the power You have determined, and by the decree You have made binding and final,
v.97: and by which You have overcome those upon whom You applied it, to grant me, on this night and at this hour,
v.98: [forgiveness for] every offence I have committed, every sin I have done, every ugly deed I have kept secret,
v.99: and every foolish thing I have done, whether I concealed it or declared it, hid it or showed it,
v.100: and every bad deed You have ordered the noble scribes to record —
v.101: those You have charged with recording what comes from me, and made witnesses over me alongside my limbs,
v.102: while You Yourself were the watcher over me behind them, and witness to what was hidden from them,
v.103: which, by Your mercy, You concealed, and by Your bounty You covered; and [I ask] that You increase my share
v.104: of every good You send down, or kindness You bestow, or goodness You spread,
v.105: or provision You extend, or sin You forgive, or error You cover. O Lord, O Lord, O Lord!
v.106: My God, my Master, my Protector, and Owner of my bondage! O You in whose hand is my forelock,
v.107: O You who know my distress and misery, O You who are aware of my poverty and need — O Lord, O Lord, O Lord!
v.108: I ask You by Your right and Your holiness, and by the greatest of Your attributes and names,
v.109: to make my times in the night and the day filled with Your remembrance and joined to Your service, and my deeds accepted by You,
v.110: so that my deeds and my litanies all become one single litany, and my state in Your service is everlasting.
v.111: My Master! O You on whom I rely, O You to whom I complain of my states — O Lord, O Lord, O Lord!
v.112: Strengthen my limbs for Your service, and brace my heart with resolve,
v.113: and grant me earnestness in fearing You and constancy in staying joined to Your service,
v.114: so that I may advance toward You in the fields of the foremost, and hasten to You among the outstanding,
v.115: and long for Your nearness among those who long, and draw close to You with the closeness of the sincere,
v.116: and fear You with the fear of those who are certain, and gather in Your nearness with the believers.
v.117: O Allah, whoever wishes me harm, wish [the same] for him, and whoever plots against me, plot against him,
v.118: and make me among Your servants the best in share with You, the nearest in rank to You, and the most special in closeness to You,
v.119: for that is attained only by Your bounty. Be generous to me with Your generosity, and turn to me with Your glory,
v.120: and guard me by Your mercy, and make my tongue eager in Your remembrance and my heart enraptured by Your love,
v.121: and favour me with Your good answer, overlook my stumble, and forgive my slip,
v.122: for You have decreed that Your servants worship You, commanded them to call on You, and guaranteed them an answer.
v.123: So to You, my Lord, I have turned my face, and to You, my Lord, I have stretched out my hand.
v.124: By Your might, answer my supplication, bring me to my hopes, and do not cut off my hope of Your bounty,
v.125: and spare me the evil of my enemies among jinn and humankind.
v.126: O You who are quick to be pleased, forgive one who owns nothing but supplication, for You do whatever You will.
v.127: O You whose name is a remedy, whose remembrance is a cure, and obedience to whom is wealth,
v.128: have mercy on one whose capital is hope and whose weapon is weeping.
v.129: O You who lavish blessings, O You who ward off misfortunes, O Light of those who feel lonely in the darkness,
v.130: O Knower who was never taught, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and do with me what befits You.
v.131: And may Allah bless His Messenger and the blessed Imams of his family, and grant them abundant peace.
